item.title: Digital Asset Overview
item.description:
Digital Asset Overview

Any piece of information stored in digital format such as images, videos, photos, documents, media files, and other digital records can be called a digital asset.

Digital assets are not limited to online media. Real-world assets such as stocks, bonds, real estate, gold, and other commodities are increasingly being tokenized and converted into digital formats. Ownership of the tokenized asset gives rights to the underlying physical asset.

item.title: Asset Tokenization
item.description:
Asset Tokenization

Asset tokenization is the process of creating a digital token that maps to a physical asset and allows the value of the physical asset to be transferred into the digital token.

This makes ownership easier to track and transfer while improving transparency and security. Digital tokens are created using blockchain infrastructure, which makes ownership tracking and transfer visible and verifiable.

Types of Tokenization

Fungible Asset Tokenization

Tokens are created for assets that are interchangeable and divisible. Examples include commodities such as gold, oil, food grains, and financial instruments.

item.title: Asset Tokenization Process
item.description:
Asset Tokenization Process

The lifecycle of a token generally follows a structured process from minting to transfer and eventual retirement.

Token Lifecycle

  1. A physical or digital asset with unique characteristics is identified.
  2. The asset is tokenized and recorded on the blockchain.
  3. Metadata or unique characteristics are embedded into the token.
  4. The token is minted and listed for sale or auction.
  5. Cryptocurrency is used to purchase the token and the transaction is recorded on the blockchain.
  6. Ownership is transferred from the minter to the buyer.
  7. After use or consumption, the token may be removed from circulation.

Burning

Burning is the process of sending a token to an inaccessible wallet address so it cannot be used again. While the token still exists on the blockchain, it is effectively removed from circulation.

item.title: Digital Asset Custody
item.description:
Digital Asset Custody

Digital asset custody means that custodians manage the wallets and private keys on behalf of the owner of the digital assets.

With external custodian offerings, the owner may not know or have direct access to the private keys. If the owner forgets their password, the custodian can verify their identity and help them regain access to their assets.

Custodians Typically Provide

  • Custodial wallets to store and manage cryptographic keys
  • Multi-signature processing
  • Approval workflows requiring multiple parties to authorize a transaction

Types of Custody

Self Custody

Self-custody is the practice of organizations storing and managing their own digital assets without relying on a third-party exchange or custodian.

item.title: Crypto Exchange
item.description:
Crypto Exchange

A crypto exchange is a marketplace where people can buy, sell, and trade crypto assets, including cryptocurrencies, fiat currencies, and NFTs.

Types of Crypto Exchanges

Centralized Exchange (CEX)

Centralized exchanges act as an intermediary between a buyer and a seller. They generate revenue through commissions and transaction fees.

Decentralized Exchange (DEX)

A decentralized exchange allows buyers and sellers to transact directly from their digital wallets without going through an intermediary.

item.title: Crypto Wallets
item.description:
Crypto Wallets

A crypto wallet is an application that functions as a wallet for digital assets. It contains components that rely on public key infrastructure (PKI).

Crypto digital assets are stored on the blockchain and can only be accessed using a private key. Your private key allows you to make transactions and unlocks the right to spend the associated cryptocurrencies. If you lose your private key, you lose access to your cryptocurrency.

item.title: Types of Crypto Wallets
item.description:
Types of Crypto Wallets

Crypto wallets can be categorized based on connectivity and custody.

By Connectivity

Cold Storage (Offline)

  • Hardware Wallet: stores private keys in hardware security modules (HSM) or hardware tokens.
  • Paper Wallet: stores private keys in printed or engraved physical form.

Hot Storage (Online)

  • Web Wallet: private keys are stored in browser extensions or web applications.
  • Mobile Wallet: private keys are stored inside mobile apps.
  • Desktop Wallet: private keys are stored in desktop applications.

By Custody Model

Wallet Type Control
Non-Custodial Wallet User controls the private key
Custodial Wallet Wallet provider controls the private key

Security Tradeoff

Cold wallets are more secure, while hot wallets are more convenient and accessible.

item.title: Fungible Assets
item.description:
Fungible Assets

Fungible assets are interchangeable and identical in value. One unit is essentially the same as another.

Examples of fungible assets include:

  • Cryptocurrency
  • Stablecoins
  • Government-issued currencies
  • Commodities represented in tokenized form

Key Principle

Fungibility means that each unit can be replaced by another identical unit without affecting value or utility.

item.title: Cryptocurrency
item.description:
Cryptocurrency

Cryptocurrency is a digital asset used to store and exchange value between parties involved in a transaction.

The availability of cryptocurrency is managed by nodes running blockchain software. Crypto wallets are used to store, send, and receive cryptocurrency.

Core Characteristics

  • Digital native asset that exists only virtually
  • Trustless and decentralized
  • No intermediary such as a bank or payment processor
  • Uses cryptography to secure transactions
  • Global, peer-to-peer transfers available 24/7
  • Not issued by a central authority or government

Blockchain Record

Cryptocurrency transactions are stored on a blockchain containing a distributed ledger shared and maintained by participants in the network.

item.title: Characteristics of Cryptocurrency
item.description:
Characteristics of Cryptocurrency

Parameter Fiat Crypto
Type Physical Virtual
Intermediary Government, monetary authority, and banks None
Portability Yes Very high
Durability Subject to physical wear and tear Very durable
Acceptance National or sovereign boundary Global via Internet
Security Moderate High
Decentralization No Yes

Summary

Cryptocurrency differs from fiat currency by being digital, decentralized, and not controlled by central banks or government institutions.

item.title: Stablecoins
item.description:
Stablecoins

Stablecoins are digital assets or currencies pegged to a stable reserve asset. They are designed to reduce volatility relative to unpegged cryptocurrencies and are useful as a medium of exchange.

Why They Matter

To serve as a medium of exchange, a currency must remain relatively stable. In fiat currencies, volatility is usually limited. In cryptocurrencies, intraday volatility can be very high.

Stablecoin Types

  • Fiat-backed
  • Crypto-backed
  • Commodity-backed
  • Algorithmic

Examples

  • Tether (USDT)
  • USD Coin (USDC)
  • Maker (DAI)
  • Digix Gold
  • SwissRealCoin
  • AMPL

item.title: மத்திய வங்கி டிஜிட்டல் நாணயம் (CBDC)
item.description:
மத்திய வங்கி டிஜிட்டல் நாணயம் (CBDC)

A மத்திய வங்கி டிஜிட்டல் நாணயம் is the digital form of a sovereign country’s fiat currency, issued and regulated by the sovereign nation’s monetary authority or central bank.

CBDCs are digital representations of central bank liabilities that are broadly accessible and usable by the public.

Benefits

  • Reduces counterparty risk
  • Promotes financial inclusion
  • Simplifies monetary and fiscal policy implementation

Types

  • Wholesale CBDCs
  • Retail CBDCs

Key Idea

CBDCs bridge the gap between traditional fiat money and digital payment systems while maintaining sovereign backing.

Insight

item.title: What is a Non-Fungible Token (NFT)?
item.description:
What is a Non-Fungible Token (NFT)?

Non-fungible tokens or NFTs are cryptographic digital assets stored on a blockchain with unique identification codes and metadata that distinguish them from each other.

Unlike cryptocurrencies, NFTs cannot be traded or exchanged at equivalency because each token is unique and represents a distinct asset or right.

NFT Use Cases

  • Digital artwork
  • Real estate and property rights
  • University degrees and identity credentials
  • In-game items and avatars
  • Domain names
  • Event tickets
  • Collectibles

Important Note

NFTs provide a public certificate of authenticity and proof of ownership, but they do not prevent copying or sharing the underlying digital file itself.

item.title: NFT Characteristics
item.description:
NFT Characteristics

NFTs are unique digital assets with several distinguishing features.

  • Unique identification and metadata
  • Stored on a blockchain
  • Proof of ownership and provenance
  • Non-interchangeable and non-divisible like conventional assets
  • Represent real or digital goods and rights
  • Useful for identity, collectibles, and digital ownership records

Key Idea

The value of an NFT lies in its uniqueness and the claim of ownership it provides on a public blockchain, even though the underlying file may still be copied.
